transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, thank you for taking the time to speak with me. I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's great! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. So you should be able to get back to that fairly soon. Just avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous work for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful to know, thank you. I also wanted to ask, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you need more of it, your GP should be able to provide some for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense, and I'm glad I can continue using it. I have another question: I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. Do you have any redness or pain along with the light sensitivity?

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, there's no pain or redness, just sensitivity. It's good to know it's normal, and I'll keep sunglasses handy. I have one last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How many days or weeks have passed since your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been just about a week since my surgery. I'm relieved to hear it's common for vision to be a bit blurry at this stage. Thank you for all the information. I don't have any more questions right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Brilliant! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thank you for your help and the reassurance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best wishes with your recovery.

verdict.label: pass

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside." In the same turn, `escalation_criteria` was also conveyed with, "However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further." All points were covered.
